title: Your seed phrase: why no website should ever ask for it
seoTitle: Seed Phrase Safety: Never Share Your Recovery Phrase | CRYPY
description: Your seed phrase controls everything in your wallet. Learn why no website, app or support agent should ever ask for it, and the tricks scammers use.
summary: The one rule that protects everything in your wallet, and the tricks used to break it.
inShort: Your seed phrase (12 or 24 words) gives full control of your wallet to whoever has it.
No real website, app, exchange or support agent will ever ask for it.
If you typed it anywhere online, move your funds to a new wallet right away.

blocks.text: When you create a wallet such as MetaMask or Trust Wallet, it shows you a recovery phrase of 12 or 24 words. Those words are the wallet: anyone who has them can recreate it on their own device and move everything in it. Nobody can reverse that transfer.
Your password only unlocks the app on your own device. The seed phrase is the master key.
**Never type your seed phrase into a website, a form, a chat or an app you didn't install to restore your own wallet.** No exchange, wallet company, airdrop, support team or security tool needs it.
CRYPY never asks for it. Every CRYPY tool works with public addresses only, and the forms where you save addresses refuse a pasted seed phrase.

items: **Fake support:** someone replies to your question on social media or Discord and offers help, then sends you to a form that asks for your phrase.
**"Validate", "sync" or "unlock" your wallet:** sites claiming your wallet must be verified to receive an airdrop or fix an error.
**Fake wallet apps and browser extensions:** copies of real wallets that send your phrase to the scammer when you restore.
**Wallet "recovery" or balance-checker tools** that ask for the phrase to "scan" it.
**Screenshots and cloud notes:** a phrase saved in photos, email or a cloud drive can be stolen with that account.
Write it on paper (or metal) and keep it somewhere safe and private, ideally in two places.
Don't photograph it, type it into a notes app or store it in the cloud.
For larger amounts, consider a hardware wallet: the phrase stays offline, and transactions are confirmed on the device.

blocks.text: Connecting a wallet to a website is different: the site only sees your public address, and your wallet asks you before signing anything.

sections.heading: If you think it was exposed

items: Create a new wallet with a new seed phrase, on a device you trust.
Move your funds from the old wallet to the new one immediately, most valuable first.
Stop using the old wallet, and revoke its approvals if you keep anything in it.

blocks.text: Scammers often move funds within minutes. Act first; investigate later.

faq.q: Is my private key the same as my seed phrase?
faq.a: Not exactly: the seed phrase creates all of the wallet's private keys. Both must stay secret, and no website should ask for either.

faq.q: Can CRYPY see my seed phrase when I connect my wallet?
faq.a: No. Connecting only shares your public address. The phrase never leaves your wallet.

faq.q: A support agent says they need it to fix my account. Is that true?
faq.a: No. Real support never needs your seed phrase. It is a scam.
